en.name: Dried daikon strips (kiriboshi daikon)
en.summary: Dried daikon strips keep about 4–8 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, and 8–12 months sealed in the fridge once opened. Damp is what ends a bag — softened strips clump, and then they mould — so keep the container tightly closed.
en.pantry: The rule is simple: keep it out of heat, out of direct sunlight, away from damp, and close the container tightly. A sealed bag in a cool cupboard keeps 4–8 months — the shorter end for a warm kitchen, because dried vegetables give up months quickly as the room warms. The strips darken from white to tan as they age. That is oxidation, not spoilage; they are still edible, but the flavour turns stronger and more sulphurous, which some cooks actually prefer in a braise.
en.fridge: Sealed, at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, opened kiriboshi daikon keeps 8–12 months, and in a humid kitchen that is the better place for it. Push the air out of the bag or use a gasket jar; the strips are thirsty and will clump and mould if they take up moisture, and they pick up fridge smells as readily as any dried vegetable. Once rehydrated it is no longer a dried good at all — squeeze it out, treat it as a fresh cooked vegetable, refrigerate it and use it within a few days.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for kiriboshi daikon, and freezing the dry strips adds little to a product that already keeps for months sealed. The freezer is genuinely useful for the cooked dish instead: 切り干し大根の煮物 portions and freezes well. If you do freeze the dry strips, seal the pack hard and let it warm to room temperature before opening it so condensation does not settle on them.
spoilage: Musty or mouldy smell, or visible mould spots on the strips.
Strips that feel limp, damp or sticky rather than dry and springy.
Clumping into a solid mass in the bag.
A sour or fermented smell after soaking — discard the batch.
tips: Reseal tightly after every use; humidity is what ends a bag.
Rinse well and soak in cold water, and use the sweet soaking water in the braise.
Buy small bags — the flavour strengthens as the strips darken.
Treat rehydrated strips as a fresh vegetable and refrigerate them.

faq.q: How long does kiriboshi daikon keep?
faq.a: About 4–8 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard, or 8–12 months sealed in the fridge once opened. The strips darken to tan as they age, which is oxidation rather than spoilage.

faq.q: Is it still good if it has turned brown?
faq.a: Yes. Darkening from white to tan is normal ageing and gives a stronger flavour. Mould, dampness or a musty smell are the real signs.

faq.q: How long does rehydrated daikon keep?
faq.a: Only a few days. Once soaked it is a fresh vegetable — squeeze it dry, refrigerate at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and cook it soon.

zh.name: 蘿蔔乾絲（切干大根）
zh.summary: 蘿蔔乾絲密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 4～8 個月，開封後密封冷藏約 8～12 個月。終結一包蘿蔔乾絲的是濕氣——變軟就會結塊，接著發霉——所以容器一定要封緊。
zh.pantry: 規則很簡單：避開高溫、陽光直射與潮濕，容器確實封緊。密封袋放陰涼櫥櫃可放 4～8 個月——偏短的那一端屬於溫暖的廚房，因為乾燥蔬菜在室溫升高時掉得很快。蘿蔔乾絲會從白色慢慢轉成茶褐色，那是氧化不是腐敗；還能吃，只是味道更濃、硫味更明顯，燉煮時有些人反而偏好這種。
zh.fridge: 開封後密封放 4 °C 以下，可放 8～12 個月；在潮濕的廚房，那裡才是它該待的地方。把袋內空氣壓出來，或改用有膠條的密封罐——蘿蔔乾很渴，一吸到水氣就會結塊長霉，吸冰箱味道的本事也和其他乾燥蔬菜一樣強。一旦泡發，它就完全不是乾貨了：擠乾水分、當成新鮮蔬菜看待，冷藏並在幾天內用完。
zh.freezer: 切干大根沒有公布的冷凍期限，而且把乾的冷凍，對一個密封就能放好幾個月的東西幫助有限。冷凍真正好用的是煮好的那一鍋：切干大根煮物很適合分小份冷凍。如果真的要冷凍乾貨，請確實密封，並等整包回到室溫再打開，才不會結露在蘿蔔乾上。
spoilage: 有霉味或土味，或看得到霉斑。
蘿蔔乾摸起來軟塌、潮濕或黏手，而不是乾爽有彈性。
泡發後聞起來發酸或有發酵味，整批丟掉。
tips: 每次用完都確實封緊，濕氣才是終結一包的原因。
沖洗乾淨後用冷水泡發，泡出來的甜水可以拿來燉。
買小包，顏色越深味道越強。
泡發後的蘿蔔乾當新鮮蔬菜處理，要冷藏。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼暗處約 4～8 個月，開封後密封冷藏約 8～12 個月。蘿蔔乾絲會慢慢轉成茶褐色，那是氧化而不是腐敗。
可以。由白轉褐是正常老化，味道會更濃。真正要看的是霉、受潮和霉味。

faq.q: 泡發後的蘿蔔乾可以放多久？
faq.a: 只能放幾天。泡開後就是新鮮蔬菜，擠乾、放 4 °C 以下冷藏，盡快煮掉。
